name: Bigelow Aerospace

summary.text: Bigelow Aerospace is a Las Vegas company founded by hotel owner Robert Bigelow in the late 1990s to develop expandable space habitats; it flew the Genesis I and II prototypes in 2006 and 2007 and built the BEAM module tested on the International Space Station under a NASA agreement. Its subsidiary Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) was the sole bidder on, and recipient of, the Defense Intelligence Agency's Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP) contract awarded in 2008, a program budgeted at about $22 million that the Pentagon confirmed in 2017.

facts.claim: A Defense Intelligence Agency memorandum states that the sole bid for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Application Program (AAWSAP) contract came from Bigelow Aerospace Advance Space Studies of Las Vegas, Nevada, and that the contract called for unclassified technical research in 11 areas with reports due in July 2009.
facts.quote: the sole bid for the contract was from Bigelow Aerospace Advance Space Studies located in Las Vegas, NV

facts.claim: KLAS-TV reported, citing documents, that the DIA posted a solicitation for bids in August 2008, that the contract was awarded to Bigelow Aerospace weeks later with an initial amount of $10 million, and that Harry Reid did not influence the selection process.
facts.quote: In Aug. 2008, DIA posted a solicitation for bids. Weeks later, the contract was awarded to Bigelow Aerospace, the initial amount was $10 million.

sources.title: I-Team: Documents prove secret UFO study based in Nevada

facts.claim: Reason, citing Vice, reported that the total ceiling of the AAWSAP contract was $22 million, of which roughly $10 million was disbursed before funding lapsed in 2010, and that Bigelow's organization was the sole bidder.
facts.quote: the total ceiling was reported at $22 million, of which roughly $10 million was disbursed before funding lapsed in 2010

facts.claim: In response to a request from Senator John McCain's staff, the DIA sent a list of all products created under the program; The Black Vault published that list together with 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs). A separate DIA FOIA response (case FOIA-00159-2018, issued March 25, 2022) reported locating 37 documents totaling 1,473 pages.

openQuestions: The page cites DIA contract number HHM402-08-C-0072; this number was not confirmed in any source found. Check the DIA FOIA reading room or USAspending.
Sources differ on when the contract ended (2010 to 2012) and whether the subject matter of the 38 DIRDs includes warp drives and wormholes; the list on The Black Vault should be read directly.
The founding year of Bigelow Aerospace is given as 1998 or 1999 by different sources, and the company's reported 2020 shutdown was not sourced here.
